Miss Roberts Mcntgomery, who married Mr. Montgomery, is a very prominent member of a very prominent family. The doctor has no children to add to this family sketch. The doctor has been very successful in his career, and has had an additional attraction, which he brought to his public career.

Doctor and Mrs. Montgomery also served the interest of the Church and of higher education, and their services were without compensation, for love of Christ alone.

Miss Roberta Mcntgomery, who married Mr. Montgomery, is a very prominent member of a very prominent family. The doctor has no children to add to this family sketch.

Doctor and Mrs. Montgomery are connected with the College history than any of the others through their son Crawford Blair Montgomery. The Doctor's long service as a physician to the Savoy College, as well as his long service as a physician in Grayson County, is ended by a train wreck at Whitesboro. His widow died in 1925.

Mr. John Thomas Ashcraft, one of the group of the small dozen young people who devoted a year or two of their vigorous and enthusiastic youth in service of Savoy College, has a brief but interesting biography. Mr. J. T. Ashcraft, son of Andrew Jackson and Ellis Gay (Winey) Ashcraft, was born in Clay County, Alabama, bama[?], and came to Texas at an early age. He graduated from Polytechnic, and in 1883 he graduated with honors at Vanderbilt University. He commenced his course of studies by reading with Dr. I. S. King in Louisville, in 1887, the subject spent a portion of 1887 at Louisville, the subject spent a period at Louisville in the spring. He graduated from a four-year medical course in Louisville in 1887, graduating in 1880 with the B. E. degree.

On a Thursday, May of January of 1879, the young doctor started out a successful career as a teacher.
